method: footer-ratio: exact_text_bytes(parquet footers, WHOLE split) x tokens_per_char(sampled). Substituted for the usual stats-ratio because /statistics is permanently broken for this corpus (see statistics_endpoint below).
hand_assembled_note: Assembled from two runs rather than one recount.py invocation, because no single invocation could produce a usable number here. Inputs: (a) artifacts/recount/_footer-finepdfs-edu.json -- a COMPLETE parquet-footer scan of all 100 files / all 23,023,372 rows, which succeeded; (b) tokens_per_char from a recount.py sampling run that reached 60 of a targeted 300 docs before the shared per-IP 429 quota cut it off, preserved verbatim at artifacts/recount/_raw-finepdfs-edu-sample60.json.

configs.text_column_note: Verified against the live schema: eng_Latn has 10 string columns and `text` is the only payload one (next-longest values are file_path ~109 chars and url ~68). No nested payload here, unlike FinePhrase.
configs.confidence_note: The heavy-tailed factor is EXACT -- a full footer scan of all 100 parquet files covering all 23,023,372 rows, a count that matched /size exactly. The headline figure is an UPPER BOUND because tokens_per_char is applied to BYTES and bytes >= chars; at bytes/char ~1.00-1.02 for English PDF text that gives 157-161B. The remaining weakness is tokens_per_char resting on 60 sampled docs rather than 300 (429 quota). tokens/char is a property of script+domain with CV 0.1279 here, so 60 docs constrains it far better than 60 docs would constrain document length -- hence medium, not high.

footer_scan.length_prefix_overhead_note: parquet stores PLAIN-encoded BYTE_ARRAY as 4-byte length + utf8 payload, and total_uncompressed_size is post-encoding, so 4 bytes per value are subtracted. A 0.016% correction.
footer_scan.no_payload_read: Footers only, via HTTP Range against 298.7 GB of parquet. 102 MB transferred, nothing written to disk.

sample.n_sampled_shortfall_cause: shared per-IP datasets-server 429 quota (~13 concurrent recount.py processes across agents), NOT a corpus defect

configs.sampling_bias_finding: The 60-doc sample's mean document length (42,009.4 chars) overstates the true whole-split mean (25,007.4 bytes/doc from footers) by 68%. cv_tokens_per_doc was 4.414, with a median of 1,171 tokens against a mean of 11,752 -- a 10x mean/median gap. This is the README's heavy-tail warning firing on live data, and it is why the footer scan was worth doing.

discarded_sample_mean_estimate.why_discarded: num_rows x a heavy-tailed 60-doc sample mean. The footer scan shows its doc-length factor was 68% too high, so it overstates by ~1.68x. An 8x-wide CI cannot size a pool. Recorded as evidence, never as a measurement.

configs.statistics_endpoint: PERMANENTLY BROKEN -- not a rate-limit, not a transient crashed job. Returns: "Error for ListColumn=fw_edu_scores: error=StatisticsComputationError(\"Error for IntColumn=fw_edu_scores_len: ... len(bin_edges=[1, 2]) is 2 but bin_edges[0]=1 != bin_edges[1]=2\")" -- a histogram bug on the unrelated fw_edu_scores column. Re-requested after the quota cleared and it failed identically. recount.py can therefore NEVER produce a stats-ratio number for this config; the footer method is the standing substitute.
configs.dolma2_to_upstream_ratio_note: vs the corpus's own token_count column (upstream mean 11,323.6 tokens/doc on the same 60 docs). dolma2 counts finepdfs ~3.8% higher than upstream. Multiply card figures by this rather than re-counting.
configs.card_tokens_note: '350B+ tokens' covers ALL 69 languages, not eng_Latn. eng_Latn is 298.7 GB of 735.6 GB parquet (40.6%) and 23.02M of 49.53M rows (46.5%); the card publishes no per-language token table. Byte-share scaling implies ~142B for English, agreeing with the measured 161B within 13%.
configs.license_detail: ODC-By v1.0. cardData license: odc-by; card 'Licensing Information' names Open Data Commons Attribution License (ODC-By) v1.0. Use also subject to CommonCrawl Terms of Use. Not gated.
configs.lineage: PDF text extracted with rolmOCR from CommonCrawl PDFs, CC-MAIN-2013-20 through CC-MAIN-2025-08, filtered to the top 10% by an educational classifier (Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 annotations; a fixed score>=3 threshold would have kept only ~2%). GLOBALLY DEDUPLICATED, unlike fineweb-edu. Near-orthogonal to CC-HTML corpora per design doc §3.1.
